pr_title: Add permissions to kibana_system for TI package transforms to support IOC expiration
pr_body: Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/94505 by adding required permissions to `kibana_system` to support IOC expiration of Threat Intel indices.
pr_comments:
> Ping @elastic/kibana-security for awareness

ACK! Thanks for the update!

Just before we merge, @andrewkroh, would it be wise to have a pattern outside of `logs-*`? If we want to place all our TI transforms there in the future, and any future `logs-*` templates and global index patterns might complicate things if it covers the transform indices as well?

Hey @andrewkroh,
As per @kc13greiner review above, I changed names of the indices with a preceding `.`. Could you please confirm if this also addresses @P1llus concern [above](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/94506#issuecomment-1489992516)? Or does it make sense to move into a different pattern altogether? If so, may I have a suggestion please? Thanks!

> would it be wise to have a pattern outside of logs-*? If we want to place all our TI transforms there in the future, and any future logs-* templates and global index patterns might complicate things if it covers the transform indices as well?

@P1llus What specifically is the concern that could cause a complication? And by "to place all our TI transforms there" do you mean the destination index name for the installed transforms? What naming conventions are you thinking?

In https://github.com/elastic/integrations/pull/5582 the convention used is `logs-ti_<name>_latest.<data_stream>` for transform destination and the integration data streams are `logs-ti_<name>.<data_stream>-*`.

IIUC Fleet should create an index template for the transform's target index. This is described at https://github.com/elastic/package-spec/blob/29cc306237b541e7c32841548c09e25dcfd19333/spec/integration/elasticsearch/transform/spec.yml#L7-L10. That template should have a priority of 200 according to [this](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/index-templates.html). So as long as the transforms destination index names don't overlap with the integration data stream naming it shouldn't be an issue. I think the inclusion of `_latest` should work to prevent collisions.

I'm not opposed to a completely non-overlapping naming convention, but there is no prior art within Fleet that I'm aware of.

That template should have a priority of 200 according to [this](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/index-templates.html). So as long as the transforms destination index names don't overlap with the integration data stream naming it shouldn't be an issue. I think the inclusion of `_latest` should work to prevent collisions.

@andrewkroh I was just concerned that any future ILM, index templates, dynamic templates or other settings that might be added to logs-* as a global pattern could affect the destination index for the transforms, outside of that I do not have any other concerns.

Hey @kc13greiner 

> @kc13greiner It's not really a "system index" as I have seen the term defined in various Elasticsearch issues. It is going to contain data that users directly access. Users will utilize it through the Security [Indicator Match](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/security/current/rules-ui-create.html#create-indicator-rule) Rules, the Security [Intelligence](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/security/current/es-ui-overview.html#_intelligence) page, and possibly Discover. Therefore I think it would be better to not use a . to indicate this is a system or hidden.

The current code has the `.` prefix added. Based on Andrew's suggestion above, could you give your confirmation that its required or not? Could you please review and let me know if thats the only change required?

@kcreddy @andrewkroh 

I have discussed with the security team and we are ok to approve without the `.` prefix on the indices. The [docs](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/index-templates.html) do warn users against using these `log-` patterns to avoid collisions.

Sorry for the confusion.

Sorry for the delay. I removed the dot `.` prefix. Could you please approve/merge if everything looks good?

issue_context.title: Need kibana_system privileges for Threat Intel (TI) package transforms to support IOC expiration
issue_context.body:
### Description

**Requirement:**
Threat Intelligence (TI) data providers generate data in the form of indicators of compromise (IOCs). The threat landscape is always evolving and therefore the IOCs need to update to reflect the current state or expired when the indicators are no longer relevant.

As a user of indictor match rules I only want to match against the latest IOCs only.
As a threat intel provider I want to be able to update or expire IOCs that my customers store.

**Support:**
- Using `latest` transform in Elasticsearch to maintain "latest" index that only contains latest IOCs and not the expired ones.

**Current Issue:**
- In current scenario, when installing the integration with the transform, following error is received: `Error installing ti_recordedfuture 1.6.0: security_exception: [security_exception] Reason: action [indices:admin/create] is unauthorized for service account [elastic/kibana] on indices [logs-ti_recordedfuture_latest.threat], this action is granted by the index privileges [create_index,manage,all]`. Reference: https://github.com/elastic/integrations/pull/5460
- It seems like the service account `elastic/kibana` which is automatically used for installing the integration/assets doesn't seem to contain necessary privileges required on destination index, which needs `index, read, create_index, delete` permissions. It also needs a `read` on source indices.
- The other permissions, namely `view_index_metadata` and `manage_transform` are already added to the `elastic/kibana` service account.

Need to[ setup required permissions onto ](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/security/authz/store/ReservedRolesStore.java#L682)`kibana_system` on all TI destination indices required to support IOC expiration using transforms.

Update: Would also need additional permissions to manage ILM on source indices. Refer: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/94505#issuecomment-1493866234
comments:
As per: https://github.com/elastic/integrations/pull/5460/files#r1142508705

Now that source indices contain duplicates, ILM policy on source indices is also needed to avoid unconditional growth of source data. Hence the `kibana_system` user would need additional permissions on source indices such as `delete_index`

review_comments: I think there should be a comment similar to L829 that states that the ILM policies for Threat Intelligence packages may include delete actions.
Added separate comments for ILM and transform permissions
